processing.extraction_tool: bsdtar 3.8.9 - libarchive 3.8.9 zlib/1.2.13.1-motley liblzma/5.8.3 bz2lib/1.0.8 libzstd/1.5.7 cng/2.0 libb2/bundled

cleaning_rules: Source CSV fields are read as text and kept unchanged under src_* columns; no source file is modified.
PM2.5 = `Raw Conc.` (µg/m³). `NowCast Conc.` is kept only as nowcast_ugm3 for reference and is never used as the measurement.

`Date (LT)` is parsed with the strict format %Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p; the original string is kept in ts_original. Local time is localised to Asia/Bishkek (UTC+6, no daylight saving) and also stored as UTC. The source does not say whether the stamp is the start or end of the hour; it is used as given and never shifted.
`QC Name` is kept as qc_name_original and standardised to VALID / INVALID / MISSING / SUSPECT (else UNKNOWN).
-999 (and non-numeric values) become NaN, never 0 (flag_sentinel_999, flag_missing_value).
Negative values are kept in pm25_raw_ugm3 and flagged flag_neg_noise; pm25_model_ugm3 is clipped at 0.

pm25_model_ugm3 is filled only for hours whose primary row has QC VALID, a real value, the expected unit and a parsed timestamp; INVALID, SUSPECT and MISSING rows stay in the audit dataset with their flags but have no model value.

Duplicate timestamps: if exactly one VALID row, it is the primary; identical VALID rows keep the first; VALID rows with different values are a conflict: all are flagged DUP_CONFLICT and excluded from the primary series (no guessing).
High readings are flagged (flag_high_value at the configured threshold; flag_local_drop / flag_local_spike relative to the surrounding valid hours) and never deleted.
The hourly table spans first to last timestamp with a row for every hour; hours without a source row are NO_ROW. Measurements are never shifted.
Gap runs, irregular 23/25-row days and duplicates are reported, not repaired.
Interpolation (linear, gaps of at most 3 h with a valid value on both sides) exists only in pm25_feature_interp_ugm3, flagged is_imputed; targets (pm25_model_ugm3) are never interpolated.

outputs.role: auditable row-level dataset (all source rows, original fields, flags)
runs of hours without a valid value
runs of hours without any source row
local dates with a row count other than 24

known_limitations: Single monitoring site; hourly values only. No coordinates are in the files (the Embassy location is approximate elsewhere in the project).
The timestamp convention (hour start or end) is not stated in the source; the 1-hour offset seen against the 2021 Clarity data (Stage 3) is not resolved here.

Conflicting duplicate timestamps are excluded rather than resolved; the cause is not documented in the source (US daylight-saving dates in the data: row counts {'2019-03-10': 24, '2019-11-03': 24, '2020-03-08': 24, '2020-11-01': 24, '2021-03-14': 24, '2021-11-07': 24, '2022-03-13': 24, '2022-11-06': 24, '2023-03-12': 24, '2023-11-05': 24, '2024-03-10': 24}).

QC `Valid` is the provider's flag and the measurement behaviour is not homogeneous over time. Minimum valid raw value by year: {2019: 5.0, 2020: -4.0, 2021: -5.0, 2022: -4.0, 2023: -4.0, 2024: -4.0} (2019 never goes below 5 µg/m³; later years contain near-zero and negative readings). Months where at least 30 % of valid readings are below 5 µg/m³: ['2020-04..2020-09', '2022-05..2022-07', '2023-04..2024-06']. Low shares are partly natural in clean-air summers, so compare winter with winter: Nov–Mar months before 2023-11 range 0.0–15.6 %, while 2023-11 to 2024-03 range 37.9–61.9 %. In some hours near-zero values alternate with ~150 µg/m³ values (e.g. 2024-02-29 22:00). These rows are flagged where detectable (flag_local_drop) but NOT removed or reclassified. The cause is unverified (possible instrument or reporting change); the periods need review before use in modelling or forecast evaluation.
Local drop/spike flags only catch isolated values relative to neighbouring hours; they cannot detect an entire low-reading period.

The archive holds yearly 'YTD' files; the 2020 and 2021 files carry an older modification date (Jul 2022) than the others (Jul 2024), so later quality-control revisions, if any, may not be reflected in every year.
Gaps are reported but not imputed in the target; feature interpolation is limited to short gaps.
Redistribution terms: the Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0, but the original provider's terms for the Embassy data are not documented in the record.
